items.title: Nick Mondello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 19, 2022
items.q: the person who would follow her or precede her in her lesson was Carlotta Monti who was W.C. Fields’ girlfriend.

ctx.x: Me too. And you had mentioned before we were recording how the tangents in the music world and how it’s all this connection and I remember seeing, “Oh Clark Terry’s on this record and he was on that other record” and all these just like musical chairs I’d have to say.

Without a doubt. One of the things that I enjoy doing, I’m sure you’re familiar with Tom Lawrence Jazz Discography, which is a great, great, great resource, especially for a historian or a writer or what-have-you. But it’s always interesting to go in and plug in a name and go back to their early days, okay? I did this recently again with Manny Klein who was a great, great, great trumpet player, great guy, great sense of humor, they’d always make fun of his nose, he made fun of his nose you know. But you go back…

just went on. The synchronicity thing also, you know there’s a lot of chance in the larger sense of the word, in the jazz world. Somebody gets — it’s like Lou Gehrig with the guy that couldn’t play first base that day, you know a person can’t make a gig, all right, they get a sub, and before you know it, if not subsequent to that but when the vocalist leaves that group and goes on to another one, boom he plucks up, you know, that player. So when you go back and you study and look at, if not study this stuff you…
